description_full: Yext, Inc. operates a platform that offers answers to consumer questions in North America and internationally. The company operates Yext Digital Presence platform, a cloud-based platform that allows its customers to provide answers to consumer questions, to control the information about their businesses and the content of their landing pages, and to manage their consumer reviews, as well as to offer customers the ability to update their information and content through its publisher network of maps, apps, search engines, GPS systems, digital assistants, vertical directories, and social networks. Its platform also enables its customers to centralize, control and manage data fields, including store information comprising name, address, phone number, and holiday hours; professional information, such as headshot, specialties, and education; job information consisting of title and description; FAQs; and other information. In addition, the company offers professional services to customize the Yext platform, such as custom building landing pages and data integrations, as well as maintenance and other services; and a digital client engagement platform for financial services. The company serves various industries, such as healthcare, hospitality, food services, retail, and financial services. Yext, Inc. was incorporated in 2006 and is headquartered in New York, New York.

financial_summary: Yext, Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $749M market cap on $447M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +6.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -108% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 75% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $53M in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.47× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 5.9×.

Management returns a meaningful 9.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and stock-based comp at 11% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insiders hold 8.3% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
